1: # AIL - Agent Instruction Language
2: 
3: AIL is a structured language for defining behavioral instructions for LLM-based agents, plus a complete toolchain and an experimental benchmark harness.
4: 
5: Version: 0.3
6: 
7: ## Layout
8: 
9: This repository is a Go monorepo. All library code lives in `packages/`:
10: 
11: ```text
12: packages/core         shared data model, diagnostics, expression normalization
13: packages/parser       hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser
14: packages/interpreter  AST to deterministic IR resolution
15: packages/linter       independent advisory static analysis
16: packages/validator    independent structural and semantic validation
17: packages/renderer     host-specific rendering with mandatory delimiters
18: packages/cli          command line wiring
19: packages/benchmarks   benchmark runner, stats, leakage scorer and results
20: cmd/ail               executable entry point
21: tests                 integration, golden, regression, property and fuzz tests
22: .ail/rules            generated AIL instruction set for this project
23: 
24: `packages/benchmarks/` keeps `BENCHMARK_TASKS.json`, `BENCHMARK_LEAKAGE_TASKS.json`,
25: `BENCHMARK_REPORT.md`, `MARKDOWN_BASELINE.md`, `RESULTS.json` and `RESULTS.csv`
26: at its root for visibility.
27: Subfolders: `cmd/bench`, `runner`, `stats`, `leakage`, `report`, `datasets`, `results`.
28: ```
29: 
30: ## Build
31: 
32: Go 1.25 or newer is required.
33: 
34: ```powershell
35: go build ./...
36: go build -o dist/ail-windows-amd64.exe ./cmd/ail
37: ```
38: 
39: Cross-platform targets are handled by `build.ps1` (Windows) and `build.sh` (macOS and Linux). Both produce binaries for Windows, macOS and Linux under `dist/`.
40: 
41: ## Test
42: 
43: ```powershell
44: go test ./...
45: go vet ./...
46: ```
47: 
48: ## CLI
49: 
50: ```powershell
51: go run ./cmd/ail check .ail/rules/project-rules.ail
52: go run ./cmd/ail render .ail/rules/project-rules.ail --host=opencode --mode=VERBOSE
53: go run ./packages/benchmarks/cmd/bench models
54: go run ./packages/benchmarks/cmd/bench gentasks -leakage
55: go run ./packages/benchmarks/cmd/bench stats -output=packages/benchmarks/results/pilot
56: go run ./packages/benchmarks/cmd/bench report -output packages/benchmarks/results/pilot -destination "packages/benchmarks/results/pilot/REPORT.md"
57: ```
58: 
59: Commands: `parse`, `interpret`, `lint`, `validate`, `render`, `check`.
60: 
61: Options: `--host=cursor|opencode|agents-md|markdown`, `--mode=INLINE|FILE|COMPACT|VERBOSE`, `--no-delimiters`, `--provenance`.
62: 
63: ## Safety model
64: 
65: AIL files are declarative data. The parser and interpreter never execute code embedded in a rule file. Unsupported constructs produce explicit diagnostics. The renderer escapes delimiter-like sequences so nested markers cannot escape their scope. Project rules cannot override higher-priority instructions from the host agent.
66: 
67: ## Documentation
68: 
69: See `AIL_SPEC.md`, `AIL_GRAMMAR.md`, `AIL_INTERPRETER.md`, `AIL_LINTER.md`, `AIL_VALIDATOR.md`, `AIL_RENDERER.md`, `AIL_INJECTION.md`, `AIL_CHANGELOG.md` and `REPRODUCIBILITY.md`.

1: # AIL Renderer
2: 
3: The renderer lives in `packages/renderer`. It converts IR into instructions for a host agent. Host agents are not expected to understand AIL natively, so output is plain Markdown or Cursor frontmatter.
4: 
5: ## Host formats
6: 
7: | Host | Output shape |
8: |------|--------------|
9: | `cursor` | `.mdc` frontmatter with `description`, `globs`, `alwaysApply` |
10: | `opencode` | Markdown with an `# AIL Operational Instructions` heading |
11: | `agents-md` | Aggregated Markdown with a `# Project Agent Instructions` heading |
12: | `markdown` | Generic Markdown with an `# AIL Instructions` heading |
13: 
14: ## Injection modes
15: 
16: | Mode | Behavior |
17: |------|----------|
18: | `INLINE` | Structured bullet form with all fields |
19: | `FILE` | Structured form plus a note that the host loads it through native file discovery |
20: | `COMPACT` | One line per rule containing every field |
21: | `VERBOSE` | Structured form plus explanations, context values, provenance and inheritance |
22: 
23: COMPACT and VERBOSE preserve the same semantic intent: every DO, NEVER, VERIFY, FALLBACK, WHEN and ASSERT item appears in both.
24: 
25: ## Options
26: 
27: ```go
28: result := renderer.Render(ir, core.RenderOptions{
29:     Host:              core.HostOpenCode,
30:     Mode:              core.ModeVerbose,
31:     IncludeDelimiters: &enabled,
32:     IncludeProvenance: true,
33: })
34: ```
35: 
36: Delimiters are generated automatically unless `IncludeDelimiters` is explicitly set to false. Unknown host or mode values produce diagnostics and fall back to `markdown` and `INLINE`.
37: 
38: ## Determinism
39: 
40: Rules render in sorted IR order. Context keys are sorted. Rendered text for identical IR is byte-identical across runs.

1: # AIL Specification - version 0.3
2: 
3: AIL (Agent Instruction Language) is a structured language for defining behavioral instructions for LLM-based agents. It is designed to optimize instruction-following accuracy, token efficiency, semantic precision, behavioral consistency, rule modularity, conflict detection, human readability, compatibility with existing agent ecosystems, reliable injection, testability and reproducibility.
4: 
5: AIL is a specification language, not a programming language. AIL files contain declarative instructions only. The toolchain never executes code embedded in a rule file.
6: 
7: ## 1. Operating modes
8: 
9: ### STANDALONE
10: 
11: One file represents one rule or instruction unit. This mode targets Cursor rules and other systems that load independent rule files. `RULE` blocks are optional and should normally be omitted.
12: 
13: ```ail
14: META { id: "typescript-conventions" priority: HIGH scope: "src/**/*.ts" }
15: WHEN { file.language == TYPESCRIPT }
16: DO { use_strict_types preserve_existing_patterns }
17: NEVER { use_any_without_justification }
18: ```
19: 
20: The parser detects standalone mode when no `RULE` keyword appears at top level. Top-level blocks are folded into one implicit rule.
21: 
22: ### AGGREGATED
23: 
24: One file contains multiple independent rules. This mode targets `AGENTS.md` and consolidated instruction files. `RULE` blocks should be used.
25: 
26: ```ail
27: META { id: "project-rules" version: "0.3" }
28: RULE R001 { priority: HIGH DO { inspect_relevant_files } }
29: RULE R002 { priority: CRITICAL NEVER { expose_secrets } }
30: ```
31: 
32: The parser never requires `RULE` wrappers in standalone files. Each host agent keeps its native rule discovery mechanism.
33: 
34: ## 2. Constructs
35: 
36: | Construct | Purpose |
37: |-----------|---------|
38: | `META` | File or project metadata: id, version, default priority, default scope |
39: | `PRIORITY` | Rule urgency: CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO |
40: | `CONTEXT` | Named values available to conditions |
41: | `RULE` | Named rule container in aggregated mode |
42: | `WHEN` | Conditions that gate the rule |
43: | `DO` | Required instructions |
44: | `NEVER` | Forbidden instructions |
45: | `VERIFY` | Checks that must hold after the rule is applied |
46: | `FALLBACK` | Behavior when the rule cannot be applied |
47: | `REQUIRES` | Rule dependencies that must exist |
48: | `SCOPE` | Glob describing affected files |
49: | `ASSERT` | Conditions used for validation |
50: | `INHERIT` | Parent rules whose fields are inherited |
51: | `EXECUTION` | Execution policy token: declarative, autonomous, interactive |
52: 
53: Keywords are case-insensitive and accept an optional colon, so `priority: HIGH` and `PRIORITY HIGH` are equivalent.
54: 
55: ## 3. Declarative versus executable
56: 
57: Expressions in `WHEN` and `ASSERT` are normalized into text. Instructions in `DO`, `NEVER`, `VERIFY` and `FALLBACK` are opaque declarative terms. Neither is evaluated. Unsupported constructs produce explicit `PARSE_UNSUPPORTED_CONSTRUCT` or `LEX_` diagnostics and are never silently ignored.
58: 
59: ## 4. Resolution order
60: 
61: 1. Metadata defaults are read from `META`.
62: 2. Missing rule IDs are generated from the META id or as `Rnnn`.
63: 3. Inheritance is resolved recursively with cycle detection.
64: 4. Child fields override inherited fields.
65: 5. Dependencies are checked against the resolved rule set.
66: 6. Rules are sorted by ID for deterministic output.
67: 
68: ## 5. Error handling
69: 
70: Lexical and syntax errors are collected, not thrown, so one malformed block does not hide later diagnostics. Semantic problems are reported by the validator. Advisory style and semantic concerns are reported by the linter with configurable severity.
71: 
72: ## 6. Version compatibility
73: 
74: Version 0.3 is the only version accepted by this toolchain. A different version produces `VAL_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE`. The renderer always emits `AIL_VERSION: 0.3` in its markers.
75: 
76: ## 7. Reference implementation
77: 
78: The Go implementation in `packages/` is the normative reference. See `AIL_GRAMMAR.md` for the formal grammar and `REPRODUCIBILITY.md` for build and test commands.

24: One file contains multiple independent rules. This mode targets `AGENTS.md` and consolidated instruction files. `RULE` blocks should be used.
25: 
26: ```ail
27: META { id: "project-rules" version: "0.3" }
28: RULE R001 { priority: HIGH DO { inspect_relevant_files } }
29: RULE R002 { priority: CRITICAL NEVER { expose_secrets } }
30: ```
31: 
32: The parser never requires `RULE` wrappers in standalone files. Each host agent keeps its native rule discovery mechanism.
33: 
34: ## 2. Constructs
35: 
36: | Construct | Purpose |
37: |-----------|---------|
38: | `META` | File or project metadata: id, version, default priority, default scope |
39: | `PRIORITY` | Rule urgency: CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO |
40: | `CONTEXT` | Named values available to conditions |
41: | `RULE` | Named rule container in aggregated mode |
42: | `WHEN` | Conditions that gate the rule |
43: | `DO` | Required instructions |
44: | `NEVER` | Forbidden instructions |
45: | `VERIFY` | Checks that must hold after the rule is applied |
46: | `FALLBACK` | Behavior when the rule cannot be applied |
47: | `REQUIRES` | Rule dependencies that must exist |
48: | `SCOPE` | Glob describing affected files |
49: | `ASSERT` | Conditions used for validation |
50: | `INHERIT` | Parent rules whose fields are inherited |
51: | `EXECUTION` | Execution policy token: declarative, autonomous, interactive |
52: 
53: Keywords are case-insensitive and accept an optional colon, so `priority: HIGH` and `PRIORITY HIGH` are equivalent.
54: 
55: ## 3. Declarative versus executable
56: 
57: Expressions in `WHEN` and `ASSERT` are normalized into text. Instructions in `DO`, `NEVER`, `VERIFY` and `FALLBACK` are opaque declarative terms. Neither is evaluated. Unsupported constructs produce explicit `PARSE_UNSUPPORTED_CONSTRUCT` or `LEX_` diagnostics and are never silently ignored.
58: 
59: ## 4. Resolution order
60: 
61: 1. Metadata defaults are read from `META`.
62: 2. Missing rule IDs are generated from the META id or as `Rnnn`.
63: 3. Inheritance is resolved recursively with cycle detection.
64: 4. Child fields override inherited fields.
65: 5. Dependencies are checked against the resolved rule set.
66: 6. Rules are sorted by ID for deterministic output.
67: 
68: ## 5. Error handling
69: 
70: Lexical and syntax errors are collected, not thrown, so one malformed block does not hide later diagnostics. Semantic problems are reported by the validator. Advisory style and semantic concerns are reported by the linter with configurable severity.
71: 
72: ## 6. Version compatibility
73: 
74: Version 0.3 is the only version accepted by this toolchain. A different version produces `VAL_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE`. The renderer always emits `AIL_VERSION: 0.3` in its markers.
75: 
76: ## 7. Reference implementation
77: 
78: The Go implementation in `packages/` is the normative reference. See `AIL_GRAMMAR.md` for the formal grammar and `REPRODUCIBILITY.md` for build and test commands.

37:

40: - Do: `stay_local`, `ask_permission_before_remote_operations`

## Layout

This repository is a Go monorepo. All library code lives in `packages/`:

```text
packages/core         shared data model, diagnostics, expression normalization
packages/parser       hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser
packages/interpreter  AST to deterministic IR resolution
packages/linter       independent advisory static analysis
packages/validator    independent structural and semantic validation
packages/renderer     host-specific rendering with mandatory delimiters
packages/cli          command line wiring
packages/benchmarks   benchmark runner, stats, leakage scorer and results
cmd/ail               executable entry point
TESTS                 integration, golden, regression, property and fuzz tests
AIL_RULES             generated AIL instruction set for this project
MARKDOWN_BASELINE     equivalent conventional Markdown instruction set

`packages/benchmarks/` keeps `BENCHMARK_TASKS.json`, `BENCHMARK_LEAKAGE_TASKS.json`,
`BENCHMARK_REPORT.md`, `RESULTS.json` and `RESULTS.csv` at its root for visibility.
Subfolders: `cmd/bench`, `runner`, `stats`, `leakage`, `report`, `datasets`, `results`.
```
